descriptions.description: Speak Business English Like an American
Lesson 20 • Talking About a Brown Noser

exercises.title: Choose the most appropriate response to the following:

question.text: 1. We'd better be careful what we say in the office.

options.option: That's right. The walls have ears.
Likely story!
Right, I wasn't born yesterday.

question.text: 2. Eric, we're going to have to ask you to take a 40 percent pay cut. But next year, I promise we'll triple your salary.

options.option: Lower your voice. The walls have ears!
Don't get too excited. Chill out!
That's hard to believe. I wasn't born yesterday!

question.text: 3. Jill is constantly flattering her boss and offering to do favors for him.

options.option: Why doesn't she butter him up instead?
Think twice before accepting favors from her.
That's one way to climb the corporate ladder.

question.text: 4. I'm giving a presentation to our CEO in a half an hour. I'm so nervous!

options.option: Likely story.
Chill out!
You're such a yes man.

question.text: 5. I spent three hours helping Rick with his financial projections, and he didn't even say thank you.

options.option: You need to look at yourself in the mirror.
I'm sure you'll think twice before helping him again.
He's trying to climb the corporate ladder.

question.text: 6. Maria works at least 60 hours a week at the law firm and always volunteers for extra work. She's an excellent employee.

options.option: She'll definitely get ahead.
Let's not talk about her behind her back.
It's a dog-eat-dog world.

question.text: 7. Paul was arrested for stealing millions of dollars from his company.

options.option: I'm not surprised. He's a real yes man.
That's one way to climb the corporate ladder.
I don't know how he can look at himself in the mirror.

question.text: 8. You're the best boss I've ever had and definitely the smartest!

options.option: Are you just out for yourself?
Are you trying to butter me up?
Isn't it a dog-eat-dog world?
